precepts.text: Under every green tree, the place where they did offer sweet savour to all their idols.
precepts.point: Groves of trees are where the nations worshipped, and powerful men still gather at such places.
precepts.why:
Ezekiel names the same places: “upon every high hill, in all the tops of the mountains, and under every green tree, and under every thick oak, the place where they did offer sweet savour to all their idols”. Under every green tree and under every thick oak, that is where they offered to their idols. Where did they sacrifice? Under the tree.

And God's judgment falls right there: “Then shall ye know that I am the Lord, when their slain men shall be among their idols round about their altars”. The slain lie among the idols and around the altars under the trees.

Now see what the sacrifice is called. Matthew 5:23: “Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar”, and “Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift”. The gift is the sacrifice. Matthew 8:4 says the same: “offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them”. Moses commanded a gift, a sacrifice.

So when the heathen sacrificed under their tree, what was under the tree? Gifts. You don't put gifts on top of the tree, beside the tree, or hang them on the tree. You put them under the tree. That is where it comes from: the gifts under the Christmas tree are the heathen's offering to their idols under every green tree.

note.label: Ezekiel 6: Against the Mountains of Israel

precepts.why:
Sword, famine and pestilence, near and far, the slain lying among their idols round about their altars, upon every high hill and under every green tree, and the land more desolate than the wilderness toward Diblath. And the end of it: “they shall know that I am the Lord.”

Hosea shows why it has to go that way. “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” The Most High returns to His place until they acknowledge their offence and seek His face, and it is in their affliction that they seek Him early.

Affliction and judgment are how we come to know the Most High. The Christianity spirit of prosperity does not know Him, for the Lord gets our attention through judgment, just as this reading shows: it is when He stretches out His hand and makes the land desolate that they know that He is the Lord.

points: The word of the Most High sets Ezekiel's face toward the mountains of Israel to prophesy against them and against the hills, rivers, and valleys, bringing a sword to destroy their high places.

note.label: Ezekiel 6: Against the Mountains of Israel

points: The altars shall be desolate, the images broken, and the slain men cast down before their idols, with the dead carcasses of the children of Israel laid before the idols and their bones scattered round about the altars.

note.label: Ezekiel 6: Against the Mountains of Israel

points: Their cities shall be laid waste and their high places desolate, their idols broken and works abolished, and the slain shall fall in the midst of them, that they may know He is the Lord.

note.label: Ezekiel 6: Against the Mountains of Israel

points: Yet the Most High leaves a remnant, some that escape the sword among the nations when they are scattered through the countries.

note.label: Ezekiel 6: Against the Mountains of Israel

points: They that escape shall remember Him among the nations whither they are carried captive, because He is broken with their whorish heart and their eyes that go whoring after idols, and they shall loathe themselves for the evils they have committed.

note.label: Ezekiel 6: Against the Mountains of Israel

points: Ezekiel is told to smite with the hand and stamp with the foot and cry "Alas" for all the evil abominations of the house of Israel, for they shall fall by the sword, the famine, and the pestilence, near and far.

note.label: Ezekiel 6: Against the Mountains of Israel

points: The slain shall lie among their idols round about their altars, upon every high hill and mountaintop, under every green tree and thick oak where they offered sweet savor to their idols, and the land shall be made more desolate than the wilderness.
Affliction and judgment are how we come to know the Most High; the Christianity spirit of prosperity does not know Him, for the Lord gets our attention through judgment.
